Appliances — the device inventory

Register the Fortinet appliances SATOM manages, keep their credentials and documentation up to date, and open each device's page for every device-level action.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view appliances.edit appliances.apply appliances.view_maintenance backups.view
📍 WhereAdministrator → Appliances in every ADOM (administrators); Operations → Appliances in a product ADOM and Global → Appliances in the Global ADOM for other profiles (URL /appliances/); each device's page at /appliances/<id>

What is it?#

Appliances is SATOM's inventory of the Fortinet devices it manages: FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate (on FortiGate, SATOM edits only from the measured GUI pages and the dry-run API console — see FortiGate). Each row stores how SATOM reaches the device (host, port, credentials, TLS verification) plus documentation you add yourself (tags, classification, model, interfaces, a datasheet). Every device-level action — discovery, console, backups, firmware, HA failover — starts from the appliance's own page.

What does it do?#

  • Lists every appliance you are allowed to see, with a live Online / Offline status badge.
  • Adds, edits and deletes appliance records. Credentials are stored encrypted.
  • Tests the connection to a device on demand.
  • Folds the several rows of one multi-ADOM FortiWeb into one device line, and keeps the device-wide actions on one of those rows only.
  • Puts a device into maintenance mode, which hides it from operators and read-only users.
  • Documents the physical side of a device: hardware or VM, model, datasheet PDF and its interfaces with their role.
  • Gives each appliance a detail page with quick actions, the Jobs on this device card and the recent audit events for that device.
  • Opens the Policy Inspector (FortiWeb) or VS Inspector (FortiADC): a live tree of every server policy or virtual server and what it references.

Requirements#

  • The device's management interface must be reachable from the SATOM node over HTTPS (default port 443).
  • An administrator account on the device. For a FortiWeb in ADOM mode, the account and the ADOM you enter decide which partition SATOM sees.
  • FortiAuthenticator authenticates with a per-user API key, not the login password. Issue one by ticking Web service access on an administrator account on the FortiAuthenticator, and store that key in the Password field.
  • If Verify SSL certificate stays ticked, the device's certificate must chain to a public root or to a CA imported in the Trust store.

Permissions#

Action What unlocks it
Open the appliance list and a device page, run Test Connection, open a datasheet, read the live HA member roles, open the Firmware Reports pages appliances.view
See the Appliances menu entry (in the Administrator group for holders of users.manage; otherwise in the Operations group of a product ADOM, in the Global group of the Global ADOM) appliances.view
Add Appliance, Edit, Delete, add or detach HA members appliances.edit. The routes check the legacy config_write key, so appliances.apply or any other edit/apply permission (for example protection.edit) also unlocks them.
View Backups backups.view

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the appliance list, device page, datasheet, Test Connection, member roles and Firmware Reports now require appliances.view (sign-in alone is no longer enough), and Upgrade, Boot Partition and HA Failover require appliances.apply instead of any edit permission. The Appliances menu entry is shown to every user with appliances.view, buttons you cannot use are hidden, FortiADC rows get the Inspector and Rediscovery icons, the vdom field is labelled ADOM (vdom), and the list's quick Edit dialog no longer clears interfaces or HA settings.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: the Appliances entry moved to the Administrator group in every ADOM. Profiles without users.manage cannot see that group and keep the entry in Fleet (Global in the Global ADOM).

🔑Permission — What users without the permission see

A user without appliances.view gets 403 Forbidden on the list and on every device page, and does not see the menu entry. The Add Appliance, Edit and Delete buttons (and the Edit link for undocumented interfaces) are only drawn for users with an edit permission, and View Backups only for users with backups.view. The maintenance toggle and the Maintenance mode checkbox are only drawn for users with appliances.view_maintenance. A device in maintenance mode does not exist for other users: it is missing from every list and its URL answers 404 Not Found.

The ADOM you are working in also scopes the list. A product ADOM (for example FortiADC) shows only that product's appliances. The FortiWeb ADOM also shows rows that have no kind. Global shows everything. See ADOMs and products.

How to use#

Add an appliance#

  1. Open Appliances (in the Administrator group; without the administrator capability, in the Operations group, or the Global group in the Global ADOM) and click Add Appliance.
  2. Fill in Name, Kind, Host / IP, Port, Username and Password (all marked with a red asterisk except Port).
  3. If the device is a FortiWeb with ADOMs enabled, type the ADOM in ADOM (vdom, optional). Leave it empty when ADOMs are off. For a FortiGate, this field is the VDOM to read.

FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate take an API key or token in Password, not a login password: a FortiAuthenticator per-user API key, or a FortiGate REST API administrator token (see FortiGate). 4. Optionally add Tags (comma-separated) and pick a Zone, Line and Department from the classification catalogs. 5. Untick Verify SSL certificate only if the device presents a certificate SATOM cannot validate and you cannot import its CA. 6. Optionally declare the device's interfaces under Interfaces — what each port is FOR (Add interface). 7. Click Add Appliance.

SATOM saves the row, records the interfaces, and provisions monitoring for the new device straight away. The flash message says what was provisioned, for example Appliance fweb-01 created. 3 metrics collector(s) and 2 threshold probe(s) provisioned. You land on the new device's page.

💡Tip — Next step

Run a Discovery on the new device. It reads the whole configuration into the local cache, records the firmware and fills in the model and interfaces.

Row actions in the list#

Each row keeps its actions on one line. Three stay visible: the lightning icon (Test Connection), the pencil (Edit, with {{perm:config_write}}) and the tools icon (maintenance mode, with appliances.view_maintenance and {{perm:config_write}}). Everything else is in the … menu (More actions):

In the … menu Shown on
Policy Inspector, Discovery / Rediscovery FortiWeb and FortiADC rows
Console, Upgrade Preparation The device row, with appliances.apply
Upgrade Firmware FortiWeb device row, with appliances.apply
A link to the device row (its name) The other ADOM rows of a multi-ADOM FortiWeb
Delete Every row, with {{perm:config_write}}

On a narrow screen the Port and Tags columns are the first to be hidden, then Host; the link above the table (N columns hidden · Show all) brings them back. See Navigation.

Test the connection#

  • In the list, click the lightning icon (Test Connection) on a row. The status badge turns Online or Offline and a toast says Connection successful or Connection failed.
  • On the device page, click Test Connection. The page shows Connection OK, or Connection failed: followed by the device's error.

Edit an appliance#

You can edit from two places:

  • The pencil icon in the list opens a short Edit Appliance dialog: name, kind, host, port, username, password, ADOM (vdom), tags, classification, SSL verification and (for administrators) maintenance mode.
  • Edit on the device page opens the full edit page, which also carries High Availability, Physical / Inventory (type, model, datasheet) and Interfaces / Connections.

Leave New Password (leave blank to keep) empty to keep the stored password. Click Save Changes.

Changing where the device is reached needs the password again. The stored credentials follow the row and nobody can read them back, so a save that changes the host, port, username or kind is refused unless New Password is filled in the same save: "Changing the host, port or username requires re-entering the password." A device with a separate SSH password also needs that one re-entered (or removed) when its host or username changes. Moving the host onto the cluster's own stored VIP is not a change of target and needs no password. PUT /api/appliances/<id> applies the same rule and answers 400.

A separate SSH login. The full edit page has two optional fields for the CLI login that SATOM uses over SSH, for example for Diagnose Log Collection and Diagnostic Battery discovery:

  • SSH user, if different from the API user: the CLI administrator, when the API user cannot open SSH. A FortiGate registered with a REST api-user is the usual case. Empty means SSH logs in with Username.
  • SSH password, if different from the API credential: the CLI password, when Password holds an API key that SSH refuses (FortiAuthenticator). Empty means SSH uses the stored password. Tick Remove the separate SSH password to remove it.

If you change the SSH user while a separate SSH password is stored, enter that password again in the same save (or remove it). The short dialog in the list does not carry these fields and leaves them unchanged.

The list's dialog does not carry the HA or interface fields, so saving it leaves the documented interfaces and the HA cluster settings exactly as they are. Change those on the full edit page (Edit on the device page); saving that page replaces the interface rows with the ones on the form.

Put a device into maintenance mode#

Administrators with appliances.view_maintenance see a tools icon on each row and an Enter maintenance / Leave maintenance button on the device page.

  1. Click Enter maintenance and confirm the prompt.
  2. The device gets a Maintenance badge and disappears for operators and read-only users. Scheduled probes and metric collection skip it.
  3. Click Leave maintenance to make it visible again. Monitoring is provisioned again for it.

The button posts the state you want, not a toggle. If another administrator already changed it, you see fweb-01 is already in maintenance mode. and nothing else happens.

Delete an appliance#

Open the row's … menu, click Delete and confirm Delete appliance 'fweb-01'? This cannot be undone. SATOM records the device's identity first, then removes the row, its datasheet and its documented interfaces. The message reads Appliance fweb-01 deleted. Its identity, configuration history and backups on the server are kept — see Administration → Stored Assets. See Stored assets.

Work with a multi-ADOM FortiWeb#

A FortiWeb in ADOM mode is registered once per ADOM (one row per ADOM, same host and port), because the login token carries exactly one ADOM. SATOM recognises rows with the same kind, host and port as one physical device:

  • The list shows the device once, with an ADOM · n badge. Click the chevron to unfold the other ADOM rows.
  • The Devices tile counts physical devices; the ADOMs tile counts the ADOM rows.
  • Firmware, the backup vault and the console act on the whole box, so they live on one row: the row whose ADOM is root (or empty), otherwise the first row by name. The other rows show a link to it instead. Opening one of those actions on another row redirects you with Firmware, the backup vault and the console act on the whole appliance, not on adom_a — they live on fweb-01.

Classification, policies and each row's credential stay per ADOM.

Read the device page#

Card What it shows
Details Kind, host and port (with a link to open the device itself when one can be built), username, SSL verification, last known firmware, ADOM (vdom), department, zone
Quick Actions FortiWeb: Browse Server Policies, View Backups, Analysis / FortiView. FortiADC: Browse Virtual Servers, View Backups, API Console. View Backups needs backups.view.
Jobs on this device The running and most recent jobs (up to 8) for this appliance, with status, progress, user and start time. Refreshes every 2 seconds while a job is active, every 15 seconds otherwise. All jobs → opens the Jobs page
Physical / Interfaces Hardware or VM, model, datasheet link, and the documented interfaces
Appliance Actions FortiWeb and FortiADC only — see below
HA Cluster — members Only on an HA cluster — see HA clusters and failover
Recent Audit Events The last 20 audit entries whose target contains this appliance's name

Appliance Actions offers, depending on kind and your permissions:

  • Policy Inspector (FortiWeb) or VS Inspector (FortiADC), and Discovery / Rediscovery — every row. The appliance list offers the same two in the row's … menu on FortiWeb and FortiADC rows.
  • Console — device row only, with appliances.apply. See Operator console.
  • HA Failover — cluster member nodes, with appliances.apply.
  • Upgrade Prep — with appliances.apply.
  • Upgrade and Boot Partition — FortiWeb only, with appliances.apply. See Firmware upgrade.
  • Restore — with users.manage and backups.restore. See Configuration restore.
  • Firmware Reports — every user who can open the page.

Every action you run on a device is a background job. See Jobs.

Inspect policies#

Policy Inspector reads every server policy live over REST and prints a tree per policy: virtual server and VIPs, server pool and back-ends, health check and web-protection profile. Raw JSON expands the full data. On a FortiADC, VS Inspector does the same per virtual server (listener, real-server pool and members, content routing and rewriting, certificate chain, WAF profile). Live mode follows each virtual server's references and reads only what it reaches; From last rediscovery draws the same tree from the last full-depth capture without contacting the device. Policies that could not be read are listed under Failed policies.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Unique label in SATOM. Two appliances cannot share a name. Yes fweb-01
Kind Product. In a product ADOM only that product is offered; Global offers all. Yes FortiWeb
Host / IP Address SATOM connects to. Yes (except a per-node HA cluster) 192.0.2.10
Port HTTPS management port. No (default 443) 443
Username Device administrator. Yes satom-api
Password Device password; for FortiAuthenticator the API key. Stored encrypted. Yes on add —
SSH user, if different from the API user CLI login for SSH sessions (full edit page). Empty = Username. No admin-cli
SSH password, if different from the API credential CLI password for SSH sessions (full edit page). Stored encrypted. Empty = Password. No —
ADOM (vdom) The ADOM this row administers on a FortiWeb in ADOM mode. Empty when ADOMs are off. No root
Tags Free comma-separated labels. Searched by the list's search box. No production, dc-a
Zone / Line / Department Picked from the classification catalogs. A value no longer in the catalog shows as (unregistered). No —
Verify SSL certificate Validate the device certificate against the public roots plus the CAs in the trust store. No (ticked by default) ticked
Maintenance mode Hide the device from users without appliances.view_maintenance. Only shown to those users. No —
This is an HA cluster (node 0) Turns the row into an HA cluster container. See HA clusters and failover. No —
Type Unknown, Hardware or Virtual Machine (full edit page). No Virtual Machine
Model Free text (full edit page). Discovery fills it in. No FortiWeb 600F
Datasheet (PDF) A PDF up to 25 MB (full edit page). Remove current deletes it. No —
Interfaces Name, Role (what it is for), Network / segment, IP, notes; the full edit page adds Type and Connected to. Saving the full edit page replaces all rows; rows with an empty name are ignored. The list's quick edit dialog leaves them unchanged. No port1, Management

The interface Role values are: Not declared, Management (GUI / API / SSH), Traffic — front-side (clients / VIPs), Traffic — back-side (real servers / pools), Traffic — one-arm (front + back), Inline inspection pair member, HA heartbeat / config sync, HA reserved management, Traffic mirror / sniffer (span), Unused, Other (see notes). Discovery fills in an interface's name, type and IP but never its role: the device does not model one. Clone and migrate workflows use the role to verify the destination.

Example#

🧪Example — Registering a FortiWeb that runs two ADOMs

The device 192.0.2.10 has ADOMs root and adom_shop.

  1. In Global, Add Appliance: Name fweb-01, Kind FortiWeb, Host 192.0.2.10, ADOM (vdom) root.
  2. Add Appliance again: Name fweb-01-shop, same host and credentials, ADOM (vdom) adom_shop.
  3. The list now shows one device line fweb-01 with an ADOM · 2 badge. Unfolding it shows adom_shop.
  4. Firmware, backups and the console are offered on fweb-01 (the root row). On fweb-01-shop a link points to fweb-01 instead.
  5. Open fweb-01 and run Discovery, then do the same for fweb-01-shop: each ADOM row has its own configuration.

Result#

  • Adding, editing, deleting and toggling maintenance write audit entries appliance.create, appliance.update, appliance.delete and appliance.maintenance. A connection test writes appliance.test (device page) or api.appliance.test (list).
  • Adding or editing a device, or taking it out of maintenance, provisions metric collectors and threshold probes for it. Existing targets are never touched.
  • The list's status badges are refreshed every 30 seconds. A cached status older than 20 seconds is probed again (6-second timeout per device).

Troubleshooting#

"HTTP 401: the appliance rejected the credentials"#

Possible causes - Wrong username or password (for FortiAuthenticator: the API key) on the appliance record. - The ADOM (vdom) field names an ADOM while ADOMs are off on the device, or the other way round. - The administrator account is locked out after repeated failed logins. - The account's trusted hosts do not include the SATOM node.

Solution 1. Open the device page, Edit, and re-enter the password (or API key). 2. Check the ADOM (vdom) field against the device's ADOM setting. 3. Unlock the account on the device, or wait for its lockout to expire, before testing again: every further attempt is another failed login.

Verification — Test Connection shows Connection OK.

A new appliance stays Offline or never syncs#

Possible causes - The device presents a self-signed or privately signed certificate and Verify SSL certificate is ticked. The connection fails during the TLS handshake, before any login. - The management port or host is wrong, or a firewall blocks the SATOM node.

Solution 1. Import the device's CA in Trust store, or untick Verify SSL certificate for that appliance. 2. Check host and port.

Verification — the badge turns Online within 30 seconds, or immediately after Test Connection.

"This ADOM can only add FortiADC appliances."#

Possible causes — You are in a product ADOM, which can only create appliances of its own product.

Solution — Switch to the Global ADOM to add another product, or pick the ADOM of that product.

Verification — The Kind list offers the product you need.

"Appliance name 'fweb-01' already exists."#

Possible causes — Names are unique across all ADOMs, including devices you cannot see (another product, or maintenance mode).

Solution — Choose another name.

"Datasheet must be a .pdf file." / "Datasheet exceeds the 25 MB limit."#

Possible causes — The upload is not a PDF, is empty (Uploaded datasheet is empty.), is larger than 25 MB, or does not start like a PDF (File does not look like a valid PDF.).

Solution — Upload the vendor PDF datasheet, at most 25 MB.

The interfaces of an appliance disappeared after an edit#

Possible causes — The appliance was saved from its full edit page with interface rows removed or left with an empty name. That page replaces all interface rows with the ones on the form. (The list's quick Edit Appliance dialog never changes interfaces.)

Solution — Re-enter them on the full edit page, or run a Rediscovery to re-create name, type and IP (roles must be declared again by hand).

A device someone else registered is missing from the list#

Possible causes — The device is in maintenance mode, or belongs to another product's ADOM.

Solution — Ask an administrator with appliances.view_maintenance, or switch to the Global ADOM.

Advanced#

Advanced Where things are stored
  • Credentials are encrypted in the database. The password is never shown again; the edit form only replaces it.
  • The datasheet file is stored on the node by appliance id; the database keeps the original filename.
  • Deleting an appliance removes everything that hangs off its database row (interfaces and other per-appliance records). Before that, SATOM records the device identity (serial, model) separately so backups on the external backup server keep an owner.
Advanced How visibility is enforced

Every user-facing list and every by-id page goes through the same visibility check: the ADOM's product scope plus the maintenance rule. A device you may not see answers 404, never 403, so its existence is not confirmed. Background automation (scheduled actions, syncs, deep capture) works on the whole fleet, including maintenance devices.

Advanced The chassis rule

Rows with the same kind, host and port are treated as one physical device. The rule is derived on every request and never stored, so editing a host immediately regroups the list. The grouping in the list is done per page (100 rows per page), so a device whose ADOM rows fall on two pages shows on both, each row still naming its ADOM.

Advanced The REST API

GET /api/appliances returns the visible appliances with their cached status and requires appliances.view; POST /api/appliances/<id>/test is the list's connection test. POST, PUT and DELETE on /api/appliances exist with the same config_write gate. Create and update refuse a kind the active ADOM cannot assign, like the list's Add Appliance. Delete does the same as the delete button: it records the device identity and removes the datasheet before deleting the row. See API.
